Conversation content on Day 53: [|User|]: Can you recommend me something?
[|AI|]: Sure, I think you might like "The Thief". It's a Japanese novel by Fuminori Nakamura. The Thief is such an accomplished pickpocket that he sometimes goes on automatic pilot, even to the point that he can't remember the source of the wallet full of money he later discovers in his own pocket. He was trained by one of the best in the business, an older man named Ishikawa. The skills he learned provide him with a good living. Now, Ishikawa reappears and offers our Thief the chance at some easy money to be earned as part of a gang contracted to perform a "sure thing" breaking and entering job. But, of course, when something sounds too good to be true, it usually is. When the surprisingly prominent target ends up dead, all the Thief really understands about the crime is that he will be lucky to survive his participation in it. It's a thrilling story!

Conversation content on Day 55: [|User|]: Hi, I'm MikeD. I had a dislike for the book "WWW: Wonder" and here's my review: If you've read "Wake" - "Watch" you'll have to read this. However, do not expect too much, "Wonder" is not even close to the preceding (both of which I considered 5 star books). The author warns us early on when he informs the reader the book was written "in and around" his consulting and scriptwriting work. Would've given a 3 star save for the pages on pages lecturing/hectoring in support of his pretty far left of center ideology. Said lectures having little to do with the plot/story. Even some really clumsy digs of a "Sarah Palin type" GOP candidate for President. Makes me think of the Ray Charles song: Good Love Gone Bad.

This book is about the war, the soldiers, and about a dog who helped to save one man's life -- not by taking a bullet for him, but by making it possible for him to live again after being wounded inside and out. Well written -- I finished it in 1 day. Couldn't put it down."
